prediction_text: Prince Rupert shall not get the honour of the wars, nor worst the Earl of Essex. Essex has the better of it: Rupert's significator is weak and disposed of by Essex's significatrix, so Rupert will be disgraced rather than honoured in this war, lose ground and reputation, and in the end quit/leave the kingdom rather than triumph. (Here 'negative' answers the question as put: no honour for Rupert.)
timing: Year scale (war outcome): Essex keeps the advantage in the present campaign and Rupert's disgrace follows in the course of the war; no single day is testified.
basis: Lilly war question: Rupert, a noble person of eminency, is signified by the 10th house and its lord the Sun — the Sun peregrine and in his detriment in a fixed sign (no dignity, no strength to win honour). Essex is signified by Venus, lady of the opposite house, who is in reception with Saturn and disposes of Rupert's significator — the adversary holds power over Rupert's planet. The Moon casts a sinister aspect to the cusp of the 10th and Venus a dexter aspect to it: the honours of the 10th are struck by the Moon and reached by Essex's significatrix, not by Rupert's. All testimonies deny Rupert honour and give Essex the better.
